reasoning.text: The render shows a generic FPGA card with four look-alike carbon-fibre 'butterfly PE' boxes and two 'K-RED' boxes floating on a bare copper rod — this contradicts the authoritative source, which is a SINGLE radix-2 CFNTT butterfly (compact_bf_v2) whose contribution is (a) a K-RED modular multiplier with ONE 14×14→28 hardware multiplier plus two shift-add fold stages and one conditional subtraction, and (b) two op21/modular_half gates that fix the INTT 2^10-scaling bug — none of which were depicted. The old overlay also floated with no ground plane (parts hang in space in the elevation views) and modelled '4–16 parallel PEs' the design does not have. I replaced the whole overlay with the real datapath grounded on an exploded logic-floor plate: 2 conflict-free memory banks + address generators, a single shared 1023-word twiddle ROM, u/v/w input DFFs, the 4-stage K-RED multiplier pipeline as distinct stages, modular_add, both op21 gates, the NTT/INTT mux and a control FSM — each carrying source-quoted spec blocks.
gaps: Verify against the next render that the exploded datapath reads left-to-right (memory→DFF→multiplier→folds→csub→add→mux) and that the heatsink does not visually merge with the overlay; if it does, raise the logic plate higher.
Add geometric variety — most logic blocks are boxes; consider capsule/cylinder cues for the DSP multiplier and rounded gates to break the box-stack monotony (geometry axis).
Model the u/v/w DFF delay chains as their true multi-stage depth (w = 2 DFFs) with visibly distinct register stages rather than one lumped box each, to make pipeline latency (6) legible.
Consider a small explicit 'bug-fix' annotation node or contrasting material on the two op21 gates so a viewer immediately sees them as the correctness fix vs. the reference.

fields.before: On-chip ROM storing precomputed roots of unity (psi^k / omega^k), reused across the rearranged loop so each factor is fetched once and broadcast over the feeder/rail to all eight multipliers.
fields.after: Single shared 1023-word twiddle ROM storing W = 9^-1·w so that 9·v·W = v·w exactly in the NTT butterfly — no post-multiply correction needed.

params.primitive_root_psi: psi = g^6 = 11^6 mod 12289 = 1945 (order 2048; psi^1024 ≡ -1 mod 12289, i.e. negacyclic)
params.j_fourth_root: j = psi^512 (order 4, j^2 ≡ -1 ≡ 12288 mod q); used as the constant rotator by the radix-4 butterflies
params.psi_inv: psi^{-1} mod q via Fermat (psi^{q-2}); INTT uses psi^{-i}/omega^{-k} twiddles together with N^-1 = 12277
params.psi_power_table_sample: entry[k] = psi^k mod 12289 with psi=1945: psi^0=1, psi^1=1945, psi^2=10302(=omega), psi^3=6320, psi^4=3400, ...; structural anchors psi^512=j (j^2≡12288≡-1), psi^1024≡12288≡-1 (negacyclic sign flip), psi^2048≡1; the omega table is the even subsequence omega^k = psi^(2k). The full 0..2047 table is generated by iterated multiply-by-1945-mod-12289 from this seed (bit-exact, no bit-reversal indexing).
params.stored: omega^k stage twiddles for k=0..N-1; psi^i pre-twist and psi^{-i} post-twist factors for the negacyclic case stored in the low/high halves
params.addressing: address = f(stage s, butterfly-block index); one fetch reused across all 8 lanes per block
params.table_contents: entry[s][block] = omega raised to the block's stage exponent (no bit-reversal indexing); negacyclic twist factors keyed by coefficient index i

before.notes:
Depth N=1024 covers every stage twiddle without bit-reversal. Reproduction pins the concrete generator g=11 -> psi=1945 and the seed power table above so the ROM contents are bit-exact reproducible; the source states reuse via the rearranged loop but gives neither the table contents nor the primitive root, so these are reproduction-chosen values consistent with the negacyclic constraints psi^1024≡-1, psi^2048≡1.
[conv] CT/DIT merged-negacyclic layout (Longa-Naehrig style): single ROM of N=1024 entries holding psi^(brv(k)) so stage s reads the 2^s twiddles at base 2^s sequentially; INTT uses the inverse table. [src] psi=1945. [calc] entries are powers of 1945 mod 12289. [source-missing] the paper's exact f(stage,block) addressing under its rearranged loop (which reuses twiddles across the loop) may index differently; the standard CT addressing above is the committed reproducible choice (only a seed table was implied). RESIDUAL TENSION: this committed bit-reversed ROM layout coexists with the paper's claimed natural-order/no-bit-reversal datapath — the bit-reversal lives only in the ROM index, not the coefficient stream, but the paper's rearranged-loop addressing that avoids even that is not transcribed.
Seed twiddle table = powers of psi=1945 mod 12289 [calc], depth 1024. Committed the standard 2^stage+block bit-reversed address that both impls assumed [conv]. The paper's actual twiddle-ROM addressing f(stage,block) under the rearranged-loop twiddle-reuse structure (loop-restructure + factor reuse to drop bit-reversal) is [source-missing] [paper] — mechanism confirmed by abstract, explicit formula not extractable.
Stores psi-powers (negacyclic). psi=1945=11^6 mod 12289 (order 2048), omega=psi^2=10302, ninv=1024^-1=12277 [src][calc]. Paper avoids bit-reversal by 'rearranging the loop structure and reusing twiddle factors' [paper]; the explicit rearranged addressing f(stage,block) is [source-missing] — impls fell back to a bit-reversed ROM, which contradicts the no-bit-reversal claim, so f(stage,block) must come from the paper body.
Address function pins the higher-confidence Impl-2 form as [conv]. psi=1945=11^6 mod 12289, omega=10302=psi^2 mod 12289 [calc]. [source-missing] the paper's rearranged-loop reuse addressing that achieves natural-order (no bit-reversal) output — current ROM still embeds bit-reversal, so the headline no-bit-reversal property is not yet met.
Stores psi powers (negacyclic twist) [src]. Reuse-via-rearranged-loop mechanism confirmed [paper:abstract]; explicit f(stage,block) addressing formula [source-missing] — committed (1<<stage)+block placeholder [conv].

after.notes: Layout/size identical to reference tf_ROM; the 9^-1 pre-scaling is what makes the factor 9 from K-RED disappear architecturally.

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic, then scribe three thin floorplan partition lines dividing the die into memory, butterfly-array and reduction/control zones; on the -X edge seat the host interface: a PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector feeding a host DMA/PCIe controller block, the boundary where coefficient vectors enter and transformed results leave. 2) Drive the controller into the forward-NTT input FIFO and natural-order output FIFO, then mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks along the left edge at 1.1 m pitch between them. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel radix-2 butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register; finally seat the four carbon-fiber radix-4 fusion yokes in the open gap between the multiplier and add/sub columns, each binding a lane-pair (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7) into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit so the eight radix-2 lanes reconfigure into four radix-4 BUs. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members, lifted slightly so they read above the pipeline-register column: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member abutting it, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame), keeping the read, return and twiddle channels on three separate heights; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the elevated rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one fused radix-4 butterfly unit onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3 -> constant j-rotator -> y0..y3 add/sub tree -> four-output register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view; add two +X dataflow arrows (mult->add/sub, add/sub->register) on the exploded unit and a thin carbon-fiber fusion-callout strut from the lanes-6/7 yoke up to the exploded baseplate so the W1->W2->W3->j-rotator->add/sub->register order and the represented fused unit are unambiguous, and clamp the finned aluminum heatsink (the exploded package thermal lid) high on its riser stub above the +X control region, sized so the twiddle ROM, address-generation and schedule blocks below stay visible in plan.
meta.after: Root everything on the PCB. Populate the board: a gold PCIe edge connector, the FPGA BGA package carrying the exposed silicon die, an in-package HBM stack on each side, a clock oscillator, two bulk decoupling caps and an auxiliary power tap; a brushed-steel heatsink base and fins cap the die. Directly above the die, an exploded logic-floorplan plate carries the synthesized CFNTT-KRED butterfly datapath (compact_bf_v2): two conflict-free memory banks with their address generators stream u/v coefficients into input DFFs, while a single shared 1023-word twiddle ROM (storing W = 9^-1·w) feeds the w delay chain. The K-RED modular multiplier is a 4-stage pipeline — ONE 14×14→28 hardware multiplier, then two shift-add fold stages (d = 3z+6q−z>>12; e = 3d+q−d>>12) and one conditional subtraction — producing 9·A·B mod q. A modular_add combines u with the product; two modular_half (op21) gates, one on the ROM output and one on the add path, derive the per-stage INTT halving that fixes the reference's 2^10-scaling bug, selected by the NTT/INTT mux. A control FSM sequences the banks, ROM addresses and the sel line; a copper datapath bus threads the stages.
